class_id: a source's zone-less local clock time is parsed with new Date() in a UTC process
feature: any scraper field whose SOURCE stamps its own observation time as a wall-clock string with no numeric offset and no timezone name (e.g. BSE `Maxdt`: "9/24/2026 5:00:00 PM", NSE demand-graph timestamps: "02-Sep-2026 17:00:13") and the scraper turns that string into a stored instant with `new Date(rawString)` / `new Date(rawString).toISOString()`
symptom: `new Date(<local-time-string-with-no-offset>)` is parsed by the JS engine in the PROCESS's own timezone, then `.toISOString()` reads it back in UTC. The prod/staging scraper runs with TZ=UTC (PM2 does not propagate a host TZ to the process), so a source string that is actually Asia/Kolkata (IST, UTC+5:30) wall-clock time is stored 5h30m AHEAD of the true instant. Downstream, any freshness/future guard comparing the stored value against `now()` then either (a) skips the write outright as "more than N minutes in the future" — losing the observation entirely, unrecoverable after the fact — or (b) accepts it when the write happens to land late enough in the next cycle that the false-future delta has shrunk inside the guard's tolerance, silently persisting a value stamped 5h30m later than it really was. `mapBSESubscription` (scraper/src/scrapers/bse-api-scraper.ts) hit case (b): BSE's day-end subscription snapshot Maxdt ("<M>/<D>/<YYYY> 5:00:00 PM") was parsed with `const parsed = maxdt ? new Date(maxdt) : new Date();` then `.toISOString()`, storing 17:00:00 UTC (= 22:30 IST) for an observation that actually happened at 11:30:00 UTC (5:00 PM IST). W-38's resolveSubscriptionSnapshotTimestamp (data-persister.ts) skipped most of the resulting future-dated intraday reads (pm2 logs: prod 465, staging 11 skips observed) and stored the day-end figure wrong whenever persistence happened late enough. The date-tz-parse-ratchet.test.ts static grep (T-327) did NOT catch this site because its RISKY_CHAIN/INLINE_RISKY_CHAIN patterns require `new Date(<bareIdentifier>)` to appear immediately after `=` or be chained directly into `.toISOString()`/`.getTime()`; the actual code was `const parsed = maxdt ? new Date(maxdt) : new Date();` — a ternary — which neither regex shape matches, so a real member of the T-327 class shipped past a gate built specifically to catch it.
first_seen: 2026-09-24 -- BSE `mapBSESubscription`, verified live against BSE's own Pubissues_GetBkbldgCatdem_ng API (IPO_NO 7992/7989/7991/7988/7987/7984, fetched 2026-09-24: every live IPO's Maxdt was exactly "9/24/2026 5:00:00 PM", the day-end IST figure). Rows already written wrong on ipodhan_staging: 273 subscriptions rows with scope=BSE_ONLY stamped exactly 17:00:00.000000 (dry-run of scripts/repair-bse-subscription-ist-shift.ts against ipodhan_staging, 2026-09-24), spanning slugs including liqvd-digital-india-ltd, unitec-fibres-ltd, s-k-offset-ltd, himalaya-nutravedics-india-ltd, injecto-polymers-ltd, century-business-media-ltd, raksan-transformers-ltd, maharaja-and-speedex-india-ltd, om-galaxy-ltd, shakti-polytarp-ltd, vama-wovenfab-ltd, vivekanand-cotspin-ltd, robokidz-eduventures-ltd, fx-multitech-ltd, dated 2026-09-12 through 2026-09-23. Intraday (non-day-end) skips are not recoverable: they were never persisted (W-38 rejected them as future-dated), so only the day-end row survives to repair. NSE's own equivalent parser (`parseNseObservedTimestampIST` in scraper/src/scrapers/nse-api-client.ts) was already fixed correctly with the same class in mind (Date.UTC(...) minus the IST offset, inlined so the T-327 ratchet recognizes it as safe) -- the class sweep for this defect found no other zone-less-IST-string site among scraper/src/scrapers (`timestamp:` writers elsewhere all use `new Date()` = scrape time, not a source-supplied observation string, which is out of this class).
fix_prs: packages/shared un-affected; scraper/src/utils/date-string-parsing.ts gained `parseIstMdyToUtcIso()` (M/D/YYYY h:mm:ss [AM/PM] -> UTC ISO, TZ-invariant by construction, same Date.UTC(...)-minus-offset inlined shape as parseNseObservedTimestampIST so the T-327 ratchet recognizes it as safe); scraper/src/scrapers/bse-api-scraper.ts `mapBSESubscription` now calls it instead of `new Date(maxdt)`. Existing wrong rows repaired by scraper/scripts/repair-bse-subscription-ist-shift.ts (dry-run default, --expect-db required, prod refused without --allow-prod, de-duplicates a shifted row against an already-correct identical row for the same ipo).
detection_check: t_source_local_time_shift (docs/reviews/detection-checks/t_source_local_time_shift.json) — flags any subscriptions row with scope=BSE_ONLY whose stored time-of-day is exactly 17:00:00, the signature this specific site's Maxdt-as-UTC bug leaves; a future member of the class (a different source or field parsed the same wrong way) needs its own predicate added to the same check rather than a new one, since the generic signature (a source-local wall-clock string with no offset, parsed by `new Date(str)` in a TZ=UTC process) differs per source's own reporting convention and cannot be checked generically without knowing each source's own wall-clock stamping habits.
